title: Red risks for a journey to the red planet: The highest priority human health risks for a mission to Mars.
organization: npj Microgravity (Nature Portfolio); authors affiliated with NASA JSC, NASA LaRC, KBR, U.S. Navy, UTMB
license_basis: Peer-reviewed journal article; copyright/licence not verified in this session - metadata and own paraphrase only, no verbatim text.
key_findings: Review (paraphrased): HRP links five spaceflight hazards to more than 30 human health risks; the authors summarise the risks ranked 'red' (highest priority by likelihood and severity) for a Mars mission.
The red risks named are space radiation effects (cancer, cardiovascular disease, cognitive decrements), SANS, behavioral health and performance decrements, and inadequate food and nutrition.
The authors propose evaluating risk through the 'space exposome' - combined spaceflight and lifetime exposures in relation to genetics - to build individual risk profiles.
limitations: Only the PubMed abstract and metadata were read; the full text was not read.
Authors' conflict-of-interest statement says views are their own and not necessarily NASA's.
Risk rankings reflect 2020 status and may have changed (own observation).
